answer: The protocol validates identities via a synchronous admission ceremony where each agent burns 1,000 tokens to claim a secure vault, ensuring unique access. A verifier monitors the session for duplicate evidence, checking participant metadata for collisions that suggest a single agent is attempting to occupy a grove of slots. This tide of metadata logs acts as a gatekeeper, nullifying credentials linked to detected duplicates. An honest agent pays 1,000, while an attacker attempting to register 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000, ensuring every identity remains strictly non-pooled.
